documents.title: Operations Meeting Minutes – Weekly Operations Meeting
documents.content:
1.1 **Treatment Works Performance**
- Maple Cross WTW operated within consent limits for all parameters. Final turbidity averaged 0.12 NTU (max 0.18 NTU). pH ranged 7.2–7.6.
- Copley WTW reported a minor exceedance of aluminium (0.21 mg/L vs. 0.20 mg/L consent) on 10 November. The issue was traced to a coagulant dosing pump calibration drift. The pump was re-calibrated on 11 November and verification samples taken at 12-hour intervals. Results to be reported to Water Quality Manager (PP) by 14 November.
- **Action 01/11/24-01:** PP to provide a written summary of the aluminium exceedance root cause and corrective actions to EH by 14 November 2024.

1.2 **Network & Distribution**
- MS reported a total of 14 bursts during the week (10 on trunk mains, 4 on communication pipes). This is within the seasonal average.
- The largest burst occurred on 10 November on the 400mm main at Leagrave Road. Repairs were completed in 14 hours. A temporary traffic light system remains in place until permanent reinstatement is completed by the Highways contractor (expected by 18 November).
- No supply interruptions exceeded 6 hours for any customer during the week. One school (St. Margaret's Primary) was without supply for 2 hours on 9 November due to a burst on the service connection; bottled water was provided.
- **Action 01/11/24-02:** MS to arrange a post-repair inspection of the Leagrave Road site and confirm reinstatement date with Highways by 15 November 2024.

1.3 **Water Quality Compliance**
- PP reported 98.7% compliance for all regulatory samples taken in October 2024. The only failure was the aluminium exceedance noted above.
- All microbiological samples (coliforms, E. coli) were negative. Disinfection residual at customer taps averaged 0.28 mg/L free chlorine.
- The annual chemical risk assessment for the raw water sources is scheduled for the week of 25 November. PP to coordinate with the external laboratory (Eurofins) for sample scheduling.

1.4 **SCADA & Telemetry**
- SC reported that the new telemetry unit at the Sundon Reservoir was successfully commissioned on 8 November. Data is now feeding into the central SCADA system.
- There were 3 communication dropouts from the remote site at Harlington pumping station. The issue is intermittent and appears to be related to the 4G signal strength. SC to investigate alternative communication paths (radio or fibre) and report back with options and cost estimates.
- **Action 01/11/24-03:** SC to provide a costed options paper for the Harlington telemetry link to EH by 22 November 2024.

Dr. Eleanor Hartley holds_position_title Operations Director. Record status: current.

---

**2. Upcoming Maintenance Schedule – November/December**

2.1 JW presented the planned maintenance schedule for the next 6 weeks. Key items include:
- **Maple Cross WTW:** Major overhaul of the No. 2 clarifier (11–15 November). This will require taking the clarifier offline, reducing treatment capacity by 25%. No supply impact is expected due to available storage and the reduced demand period.
- **Copley WTW:** Replacement of the chlorine dosing skid (18–22 November). A temporary dosing arrangement will be in place. PP confirmed that this is acceptable from a water quality perspective, with additional daily residual checks during this period.
- **Sundon Reservoir:** Cleaning of the contact tank (2–6 December). This will reduce storage capacity but is not expected to impact supply.
- **Various pumping stations:** Routine servicing of pumps and generators. Details are in the attached schedule (Appendix A).

3.3 TH raised a concern regarding the clarity of the shift handover log. The current template has been in use for several years and does not always capture the status of ongoing maintenance work. JW agreed that the handover log could be improved and suggested aligning it with the planned maintenance schedule. EH asked TH and JW to meet outside the meeting and propose a revised template for review at next week’s meeting.

3.4 PP reminded the group that the annual chemical risk assessment for raw water sources is scheduled for the week of 25 November. She will coordinate with Eurofins for sample scheduling. The OCR team should be aware that additional samples may be flagged in the system during that week and that results will be entered by the laboratory directly.

**Decision 03/11/24-01:** The OCR shift pattern of 3 shifts per day will remain unchanged for the foreseeable future. EH confirmed that no changes are planned to the 24/7 coverage model.

**Action 03/11/24-01:** TH to maintain a manual call-out log for the OCR and provide a summary at next week’s meeting. Due: 26 November 2024.

**Action 03/11/24-02:** TH and JW to develop a revised shift handover log template and present it at next week’s meeting. Due: 26 November 2024.

**4. Incident Report – Burst on High Street, Leighton Buzzard (16 November)**

4.1 DO reported on the burst water main that occurred on High Street, Leighton Buzzard, on Saturday 16 November. The burst was reported at 07:40 via the customer call centre and was attended by the on-call crew by 08:15. The main was isolated at 08:30 and repairs were completed at 14:10. Supply was restored to all affected properties by 15:00.

Operations Control Room operates_24_7_shifts 3 shifts per day. Record status: current.

4.2 The burst affected approximately 40 properties. Customers were notified via the LWWA website and social media channels. DO noted that the customer call centre received 22 calls regarding the incident, all of which were logged and closed out by the end of the day.

4.3 PP confirmed that water quality samples were taken from the affected area following the repair. All samples were satisfactory, with no bacteriological failures. The usual flushing and disinfection procedures were followed, and the Environmental Health Officer was notified as a precaution.

4.4 DO raised a concern about the age of the main. The section that failed is a 100 mm cast iron pipe installed in the 1950s. This area is not currently included in the capital replacement programme. EH asked DO to provide a list of similar cast iron mains in the area so that the risk can be assessed and prioritised for future investment.

**Action 03/11/24-03:** DO to provide a list of cast iron mains in the Leighton Buzzard area, with an indication of their condition and risk, to EH by 26 November 2024.

---

**5. Compliance Update – Monthly Water Quality Report (October)**

5.1 RG presented the monthly compliance summary for October 2024. The report covers all water quality parameters required under the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016. The overall compliance for the month was 99.8%, with one failure recorded.

5.2 The failure was for aluminium at the Maple Cross WTW. The sample was taken at the treatment works outlet on 14 October and showed a concentration of 210 µg/L, against the prescribed concentration of 200 µg/L. The exceedance was attributable to a temporary disruption in the coagulation process, which was rectified within the day. Subsequent samples from the same point and from the distribution system were all within the standard.

2.1 NS reported that the network had operated without unplanned supply interruptions during the past week. Reservoir levels across the Luton and Dunstable zones remained within normal operating ranges.

2.2 A planned pressure-management valve replacement at the Poynters Road district metering area was completed on 21 November. The work was carried out overnight and no customer supply interruptions were reported.

2.3 NS noted that two minor leaks had been repaired during the week, one at Hart Hill and one at Sundon Park. Both were on 75 mm PVC mains and were repaired within the target response time. No further action required.

2.4 DO asked NS to confirm that the temporary bypass installed at the Grovebury Road site remains in place and is being inspected weekly. NS confirmed that inspections are up to date and that the bypass will remain in service until the permanent repair is scheduled.

---

**3. Asset Condition and Maintenance**

3.1 EH provided an update on the routine maintenance programme. All planned maintenance for November had been completed, with the exception of the annual service of the standby generator at the Sundon booster station, which has been rescheduled to 3 December due to availability of the specialist contractor.

3.2 EH raised a concern regarding the condition of the air valves on the Toddington to Luton trunk main. A condition survey carried out in October identified three air valves that are showing signs of corrosion and require replacement. EH proposed that the replacements be added to the maintenance schedule for January 2025.

3.3 DO asked EH to provide a cost estimate for the air valve replacements and to confirm whether the work could be combined with any other planned work on the trunk main. EH agreed to provide the estimate by the end of the week.

**Action 26/11/24-01:** EH to provide cost estimate for replacement of three air valves on Toddington to Luton trunk main and confirm whether the work can be combined with other planned works. Due: 29 November 2024.

3.4 AB noted that the capital replacement programme for 2025/26 is still subject to final approval by the Board. EH confirmed that the list of cast iron mains requested at the previous meeting would inform the prioritisation of any additional schemes.

**RE: ABSTRACTION LICENCE NO. AL/2024/118 – RUTLAND WATER RESERVOIR RAW WATER ABSTRACTION**

Further to your application dated 5 September 2023 and subsequent correspondence, I am writing to confirm that the Environment Agency has issued abstraction licence AL/2024/118 to the Lakeside Water Works Authority (the Licence Holder) for the abstraction of raw water from Rutland Water Reservoir. The Environment Agency's correspondence confirms it issued abstraction license AL/2024/118. Record status: current.

This licence is issued under Section 24 of the Water Resources Act 1991 (as amended) and in accordance with the Water Abstraction and Impounding (Exemptions) Regulations 2006. It is valid from 20 January 2024 until 19 January 2029, unless revoked, varied, or suspended in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

The licence permits the abstraction of raw water from the reservoir at National Grid Reference SK 884 073, at a maximum daily rate of 180 megalitres (ML/day) and a maximum annual quantity of 45,000 megalitres. The full conditions of the licence are set out in the attached Schedule, which forms part of this licence. A summary of the key conditions is provided below for your convenience.

**Condition 1 – Points of Abstraction**

Abstraction shall only take place at the existing intake structure at the north-east arm of Rutland Water Reservoir, as detailed on Plan Reference LWWA/2023/114, attached to this licence. The Licence Holder shall not construct or operate any additional abstraction point without prior written consent from the Environment Agency.

**Condition 2 – Maximum Quantities**

2.1 The maximum quantity of water abstracted under this licence shall not exceed 180 ML/day, measured as a daily mean.

2.2 The maximum quantity of water abstracted in any consecutive 12-month period shall not exceed 45,000 ML.

2.3 Abstraction shall be reduced to 150 ML/day between 1 June and 31 August inclusive in any year, unless the water level in the reservoir is above 84.20 mAOD at the principal datum point, in which case the full licensed quantity may be abstracted.

**Condition 3 – Flow and Level Conditions**

Abstraction under this licence shall cease when the water level in Rutland Water Reservoir falls below 83.50 metres above Ordnance Datum (mAOD) at the reservoir's principal datum point. The Licence Holder shall install and maintain a continuous water level recorder at the datum point and shall provide the Environment Agency with remote telemetry access to the level data.

**Condition 4 – Compensation Flow**

The Licence Holder shall ensure that a minimum compensation flow of 8 ML/day is maintained in the River Gwash downstream of the reservoir dam at all times. The compensation flow shall be measured at the gauging station at Tinwell (National Grid Reference TF 002 063).

**Condition 5 – Monitoring and Reporting**

5.1 The Licence Holder shall provide to the Environment Agency, on a quarterly basis, a return of the total volume of water abstracted under this licence during the preceding quarter. Returns shall be submitted within 28 days of the end of each calendar quarter, using the Environment Agency's standard abstraction return form (WR320).
